items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I was at his house quite often... William Smith met Joe Smith and invited him to come to his house for a session one night after the show. I was there with bells on because Smittie had told me what a great horn player Joe Smith was

ctx.x: My father was not happy with me because I was not working and eventually told me that I would have to get a job. His buddy, Mr. Tarleton, who had been part-owner of the dry cleaning and pressing shop where we had stayed on Walnut Hills, was now the head porter at the main telegraph office up-town on the 4th Street and told my father that I could get a job there, so I started working and stopped hanging around with Green and William. I still practised my horn. Every other week, I had to go to work early and I…
I worked at the Western Union for quite a few months and used to see and hear William Smith, the pianist, very often because he was a professional musician and I was a beginner.

August came and every year, a certain majority of the population of Centerville went camping for one week. Those that could not stay the whole week could come for a day or two. These encampments were always on some rich white farmer's land near a creek that was deep enough to swim and to fish. There was a tent used as a dining room, where the women and girls slept, one for the men and boys.
